title: Let the failure mode itself narrow the search
explanation: `reportd-log hello` followed by `cat /var/log/reportd/reportd.log` doesn't just return empty — `cat` errors with "No such file or directory", even though `ls /var/log/reportd/` lists `reportd.log` right there. A path that's listed by `ls` but unreadable by `cat` is a strong hint you're looking at a symlink, not a regular file.

title: Follow the symlink to where it actually points
explanation: `ls -l /var/log/reportd/reportd.log` confirms it's a symlink, pointing at `/var/log/reportd-archive/2026-06-01.log`. Checking the target directory itself — `ls -ld /var/log/reportd-archive` — shows that directory doesn't exist at all, not just the file inside it.

title: A missing target directory fails differently than a symlink to /dev/null
explanation: When a symlink's target directory doesn't exist, the `open()` call needed to append to it fails outright with ENOENT — there's nowhere for the file to even be created. That's a different failure mode from a symlink to `/dev/null` (where every write always succeeds and is silently discarded); here, every write actually errors, and reportd's logging wrapper is written to swallow that error so a logging hiccup never crashes the app itself.

title: Trace the missing directory back to a plausible real-world cause
explanation: A path like `/var/log/reportd-archive` disappearing entirely, while a symlink still points into it, is exactly what happens when a separate log-archive mount or volume gets decommissioned or unmounted and nobody chases down every symlink that referenced it.

title: Fix by pointing logging at something that actually exists
explanation: Either restore the original intent (`sudo mkdir -p /var/log/reportd-archive` then `sudo touch` the symlink's target so it resolves), or simplify by dropping the indirection entirely: `sudo rm /var/log/reportd/reportd.log && sudo touch /var/log/reportd/reportd.log` makes the log path a real file directly, with no dependency on an archive location that may vanish again.

title: Verify with the exact command that first exposed the bug
explanation: `reportd-log test && cat /var/log/reportd/reportd.log` now shows the line — proving the same `cat` that previously errored with "No such file or directory" succeeds cleanly.
